description: Write a new memory/research note into the shared Second Brain vault so future sessions, in this or any other project, can recall it later. Only for a genuine, reusable learning: a fact, pattern, constraint or decision that would change future behavior or save someone from re-deriving it. Not for routine task completions, raw output or status updates (the task queue records those). Test: would a future session be worse off without this note? If not, skip it. Prefer updating an existing relevant note over creating a near-duplicate one (use brain_search first, then brain_node_update). Creates a new note and never overwrites an existing one (a title clash gets a numbered filename). Returns { success, id, title, type, version }; keep the id to refer to the note later.

agent.description: Name of the calling project or agent; the note is stored under agents/<agent>/, which keeps each project's notes together. Same filename rules as title, so no slashes. If omitted, the note is stored at the vault root and its agent is recorded as "unknown".

content.description: Markdown body. Link related notes with [[Note Title]] so recall can follow the graph. Never include secrets, credentials or personal data: notes are plain files and may be synced to git.

importance.description: How long the note stays prominent in recall, 1 to 10. Recency only re-ranks, so old notes are never hidden, but 8-10 fades over months, 5-7 (default) over weeks, and 1-4 within days.

tags.description: Short lowercase labels, e.g. ["database", "cache"]. Used by search and filtering.

title.description: Specific, searchable title that becomes the note's filename, e.g. "Decision - Use SQLite for the cache". Must not contain : / \ ? * " < > | , start or end with a space, or end with a period; invalid titles are rejected with the reason.

type.description: Kind of note: decision (a choice and its reason), insight (a non-obvious finding or fix), research (gathered findings), memory (general fact), note (anything else).

name: brain_remember
title: Save a memory
